name: Twelve rational points with many three-point lines (orchard problem)
description: construct() -> exactly 12 distinct integer points [x, y] with |x|, |y| <= 10^30 (any rational configuration can be scaled to integers). Maximize the number of lines containing exactly three of the points, computed exactly; the optimum is 19. The real maximum for 12 points is 19, and the group law on a rational cubic with 12-torsion realizes it with rational points, so the rational optimum is also 19.

sources.locator: Ben Green and Terence Tao, On Sets Defining Few Ordinary Lines (2013). Crossref records inspected (Green-Tao 2013; Burr-Grünbaum-Sloane 1974); OEIS A003035 inspected: maximal numbers of 3-point lines for n <= 14 with a(12) = 19, a(15) in {31, 32}; Erdős Problem #669 page inspected. A local test builds 12 rational torsion points of an elliptic curve with a 12-torsion point, which realize 19 lines. The real maximum for 12 points is 19, and the group law on a rational cubic with 12-torsion realizes it with rational points, so the rational optimum is also 19.
Erdős Problem #669 (open); statement, history and current bounds reviewed 2026-09-24.
